name: Monzen-Nakacho
tagline: Eight minutes to Otemachi, and the highest density of owner-run restaurants in the Fukagawa area. The catch is the Tozai Line in the morning.
summary: The Tokyo Metro Tozai Line reaches Otemachi in 8 minutes and Nihonbashi in 5. The Oedo Line reaches Roppongi and Shinjuku without a change. The neighbourhood grew up as the approach to the Tomioka Hachimangu shrine and the Fukagawa Fudodo temple, and it has the highest density of owner-run restaurants in the Fukagawa area; for eating out at night, Kiyosumi-Shirakawa and Morishita are not in the same league. In exchange, the Tozai Line in the morning ranks among the most crowded stretches in the government's own published figures, and whether you can accept riding it every day is the biggest question here.

faces.morning: Whether you can face this Tozai Line every morning largely decides whether you live here. Trains arrive full from the Nishi-Funabashi direction, and getting a seat at Monzen-Nakacho essentially does not happen. Switching to the Oedo Line eases the crowding considerably, but it is a detour towards Otemachi. Outside the station from seven onwards, people come out of the gates and head for the platforms without stopping.
faces.daytime: The temple approach and the shopping street are open, and there are people about in the afternoon. It does not fall silent the way Kiyosumi-Shirakawa does; voices and bicycles are constant. Older residents and visitors mix.
faces.night: Restaurants stay open later here than anywhere else in the Fukagawa area. Izakaya and owner-run places are open past 23:00, so you can eat on the way home. It is lively without the noise of an entertainment district, closer to a settled street of bars.
faces.weekend: The monthly temple market and events at Tomioka Hachimangu bring far more people. During the Fukagawa Hachiman festival the whole neighbourhood turns to the festival for days, which does not suit anyone after quiet. Ordinary weekends are calm.

terrain.note: Low ground near the mouth of the Sumida River, about 1 m above sea level, with only 3 m of variation within 800 m. You can cycle to Nihonbashi and Ginza without effort, and as at Kiyosumi-Shirakawa and Morishita a pushchair is easy. This is an advantage the whole Fukagawa area shares.

exits.name: Exit 1
exits.character: Towards the temple approach and the shopping street. Restaurants and everyday shops gather here; this is the centre of daily life, and it is lit at night.

exits.name: Exits 2 and 3
exits.character: Blocks of flats line the main roads. Convenient, but rooms facing the road let the traffic in.

exits.name: Exits 5 and 6
exits.character: Housing along the canal, quiet even during the day. Further from the bustle by the station, so fewer people are about at night.

residents: A high share of households who have lived in Fukagawa for generations; the neighbourhood association is run actively and many residents take part in the festival. In recent years more people living alone and dual-income couples have moved in for the access to central Tokyo, but the association's officers and the running of the festival are still in the hands of long-standing residents. How far you get involved in the festival and the association is not entirely yours to decide, and whether that suits you changes how the place feels to live in.
housingStock: Mid- and high-rise blocks near the station; a little further out, timber houses and low-rise flats mixed together. There are few converted warehouses of the kind found at Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, and ordinary blocks make up most of the stock. Within the Fukagawa area, the choice of newer buildings here is comparatively good.
hazards: On the national hazard map, for the flood scenario based on the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside it. For storm surge, all nine points fall in the 0.5 to 3 m projection too. Even within the Fukagawa area, the projected areas for both flood and storm surge spread right around this station. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
stationNote: The Tozai Line platform is comparatively shallow, but the Oedo Line is deep, and changing between them means a long walk underground. The two sets of gates are far apart despite the shared station name, so decide which line you will use according to which direction you live in. Morning delays on the Tozai Line are chronic, which is worth allowing for if you use it daily.
nightWalk: Because the restaurants stay open late, the way from the station towards the shopping street is lit and busy at night. Of the Fukagawa area, this is where walking home at night is least of a worry. One street back from Eitai-dori, though, and along the canal, the foot traffic stops.
rentReason: Rent is low given that Otemachi is 8 minutes away. The reasons are that this is low ground with flood and storm surge risk, that there is no large shopping complex, and that the Tozai Line's morning crowding is a clear negative. Put the other way round, for anyone who can accept that crowding, this is a place where the rent is good value for the location.

rentRange.note: Mid- and high-rise blocks near the station and timber or low-rise buildings a little further out differ a great deal in rent. Along Eitai-dori the convenience pushes the market up, but it is traded against traffic noise. Within the Fukagawa area, Monzen-Nakacho is the most expensive, then Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, then Morishita.

family: The grounds of Tomioka Hachimangu and Fukagawa Park are within walking distance, and Kiba Park is reachable by bicycle. The ground is flat, so a pushchair is easy. Because the festival and the neighbourhood association are active, adults nearby still know the local children by sight. Nursery vacancies and school catchments change by year and by address, so check Koto City's current information for each flat. Allow for the fact that the Tozai Line's morning crowding is considerably harder once you are boarding it after a nursery drop-off.
medical: Within walking distance of the station there are 5 clinics and 2 pharmacies, which is on the low side for the Fukagawa area. Hospitals that admit inpatients include Shuseikai Kiba Hospital and Ishikawajima Memorial Hospital, both about 1.1 km away. A bicycle widens the range considerably. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.

alternatives.note: If you want to avoid the Tozai Line's crowding, choose Kiyosumi-Shirakawa. The Hanzomon and Oedo Lines make for a comfortable commute and run direct towards Shibuya. After 20:00, though, almost all the restaurants are shut and the choice for eating out shrinks sharply.
If you want to hold the rent down, choose Morishita. Some places there stay open late, and Shinjuku is direct. Otemachi needs one change, so the commute is shorter from Monzen-Nakacho.

outlook: No large redevelopment is on the horizon, and the character of a temple-gate town looks set to remain. Development towards Toyosu and Toyocho may make the Tozai Line's crowding worse, so expect the commute to stay as it is or deteriorate rather than improve.

residentComment: Of the three stations in the Fukagawa area, only Monzen-Nakacho has the restaurants to go out and eat at night. Being able to eat somewhere on the way home is worth more once you live here than you would guess. The Tozai Line in the morning really is hard, though, and underestimating it means the tiredness of a packed train every morning piles up. Switching to the Oedo Line is possible but a detour, so unless you commute towards Otemachi or Nihonbashi, Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is easier on balance. That this is low ground, and inside the storm surge projection, is best looked at separately from how pleasant the place feels.

neighbours.note: 536 m away in a straight line. It takes 3 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Monzen-Nakacho.
1017 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Monzen-Nakacho.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 5 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The number of points that fall inside the projected inundation area is about average for a station in the 23 wards.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.exits: The shopping street and the restaurants sit by exit 1; exits 5 and 6, on the Oedo Line side, come out into housing along the canal. Foot traffic at night is heaviest by exit 1.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make: 永代通り runs 2 m away.
